findings.title: Float16Array lastIndexOf bypasses resize-guard leading to OOB read
findings.message: In `LastIndexOfValueImpl`, a special-case branch introduced to handle 0 == -0 semantics for Float16Array (where both +0 and -0 share different bit patterns) returns early using `start_from` as a raw array index without first re-checking the current array length. The `start_from` value is computed by the JavaScript engine from the caller-supplied `fromIndex` argument via `ToInteger`, which can invoke user-defined `valueOf()` methods. If such a method shrinks the backing resizable ArrayBuffer (RAB) — e.g., via `ab.resize(0)` — then `start_from` can exceed the new array length. The early-exit do-while loop then computes `data_ptr + k` where `k >= typed_array_length`, constituting an out-of-bounds read on the underlying backing store. The general code path (for other element types or non-zero search values) is protected by a post-conversion bounds adjustment block that re-reads `typed_array->GetLength()` and clamps `start_from` accordingly, but the Float16 zero special case short-circuits before reaching that guard.

related_locations.description: The bounds re-check that is bypassed: re-reads typed_array_length and clamps start_from after potential side effects from ToTypedSearchValue/ToInteger
Regression test demonstrating the exploit: valueOf() resizes the RAB to 0 while lastIndexOf(0, evil) computes fromIndex

findings.suggestion: Move the Float16 zero-equality check inside the main loop that runs after the `start_from >= typed_array_length` bounds adjustment. Use `if constexpr (IsFloat16TypedArrayElementsKind(Kind))` inside the loop body so the check is compiled away for non-Float16 element kinds, preserving performance while ensuring `start_from` has already been clamped to the current (possibly shrunk) array length before the loop begins.

ground_truth.root_cause: When adding the Float16 0-equality special case in `LastIndexOfValueImpl`, the author placed the new branch in the same `else if` chain used to handle NaN/Infinity before the `ToTypedSearchValue` call, and before the post-conversion bounds re-check block (`start_from >= typed_array_length`). This means the Float16 zero path exits early using a potentially-stale `start_from` that was derived from user-observable JS (the `fromIndex` argument's `ToInteger` conversion), without accounting for RAB resizing side effects that may have occurred during that conversion.
